clue.text: Troublemakers making very little money in fraudulent activities

indicators.note: in says the small coin goes inside the word for the frauds

parts.note: scams are frauds or swindles
P, a penny, is the smallest amount of British money

explanation.surface: Petty criminals scraping a pittance from their swindles.
explanation.walkthrough: P (a penny, the smallest British coin) goes inside SCAMS; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous rascals, people who stir up bother.

clue.text: Applauding first of competitors overtaking others on the track?

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word competitors

parts.note: in a race, lapping means passing rivals a whole circuit behind

explanation.surface: A leading runner going past the back-markers to a round of cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: C (the first letter of 'competitors') is followed by LAPPING, which is what a runner does when they overtake rivals a full lap behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is striking the hands together to show approval, which is what applause is.

clue.text: French film director sent up part of Cinderella Man

indicators.note: sent up says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A French director mocks a Hollywood boxing film.
explanation.walkthrough: ELLAM sits inside 'CinderELLA Man'; 'sent up' turns it upwards, as this is a down clue, giving MALLE. Louis Malle directed Au Revoir les Enfants.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Malle was a celebrated French filmmaker of the New Wave era.

clue.text: Rock sound associated with the Beach Boys?

parts.note: read the band's name as belonging to the beach, the shore's own material: sand's
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Asking what rock music the Californian surf band played.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beach Boys' sound becomes the beach's tone: SAND'S TONE, with sand standing in for the beach. 'associated with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of compacted grains of sand.

clue.text: Famous people lacking essential furniture?

parts.note: having no means lacking
tables are basic items of furniture in a home

explanation.surface: Celebrities whose homes are bare of the basic furnishings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as NO TABLES, a room lacking a key bit of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Notables are prominent, well-known persons.

clue.text: Tonight her man is wandering somewhere in central England

indicators.note: wandering says the letters of the preceding words stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's partner is out roaming this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges the fifteen letters of TONIGHT HER MAN IS; Nottinghamshire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottinghamshire is an English county in the East Midlands, near the middle of the country.

clue.text: Port one stored in barrels

indicators.note: stored in puts the numeral inside the casks

parts.note: tuns are large casks for wine or beer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single bottle of fortified wine kept in casks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine, which fits barrels; it is a seaport. I goes inside TUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis, capital of Tunisia, is a harbour city on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Local worker, a lawyer?

definitions.meaning: a local is a British pub, so this is someone serving drinks
barristers belong to the Bar, so a lawyer is a person of the Bar

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a pub employee might be a solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a pub server behind the counter; the other treats a barrister, called to the Bar, as a person of the legal profession.

clue.text: Periods identified in record book

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Eras logged in an archive volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identified in' is a link. An epact is the number of days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year.
explanation.definitionFit: Epacts are spans of days measured between solar and lunar calendars, so they are periods of time.

clue.text: Take sweetheart to northern town

parts.note: darling is a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.surface: Bringing a lover up to the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is an instruction joining the pieces. Darlington is a market town in County Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is a large market settlement in north-east England.

clue.text: Study musical instrument's sound

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a reed is a pipe or woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: Researching what a particular instrument sounds like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like part of the musical picture, but it signals that REED, said aloud, gives the spelling READ.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject, in British usage, is to study it at university.

clue.text: A youngster mostly suppresses urge for some winter fun

indicators.note: suppresses pictures the shortened child sitting on top of the urge to hold it down, so the pieces stay side by side

parts.note: to press is to urge strongly

indicators.note: mostly says the word for a child loses its final letter

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A child holding back an impulse to go and play in the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppresses' is a placing signal: the shortened child sits on top of, and so after, the urge. 'mostly' drops the last letter of the child word.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising that follows a day on the slopes, a winter pleasure.

clue.text: Dealt with second part of play, say?

indicators.note: say signals the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: Scene Two is the second section of an act in a play

explanation.surface: Asking whether the second section of a drama has been handled.
explanation.walkthrough: SCENE TWO said aloud sounds like SEEN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen to has been attended to or handled.

clue.text: Problem when son gets stuck on horse

indicators.note: gets stuck on, in an across clue, puts the boy's letter in front of the horse

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Trouble when a boy is glued to his mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem' and 'stuck' both suggest difficulty; 'gets stuck on' just places S before NAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected obstacle or drawback.

clue.text: Greek dancer arranged to collect European work permit

indicators.note: to collect means the rearranged letters gather in one more letter
arranged says these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek dancer sorting out the paperwork to work in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: GR plus DANCER, rearranged by 'arranged', gives GRENCARD, which collects E to make GREENCARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A green card is the US permit letting a foreign national live and be employed there.

clue.text: Player is trashed at first by newspaper

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical speaking for a group

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word trashed

explanation.surface: A footballer slated in the opening lines of a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets ORGAN beside IS and T (the first of 'trashed'). 'Player' means a musician, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist is a musician who plays the church instrument.

clue.text: Who's skilled in making contacts, a trawlerman?

definitions.meaning: one who is good at building a web of useful acquaintances
a fisherman hauling nets is, read literally, a worker with nets

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fisherman is good at building connections.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person adept at cultivating professional connections; the other reads the word as a labourer using fishing nets.

clue.text: Artist exhibited topless outfit for bride

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is removed, the top in a down clue

parts.note: a trousseau is the clothes a bride gathers for her marriage

explanation.surface: A painter showing a revealing wedding garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibited' is a link. Henri Rousseau was a French painter of jungle scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau was a French post-impressionist painter.

clue.text: Terrible gutless actors in TV programme

indicators.note: gutless removes the innards of the word terrible, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: a cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A dreadful, spineless troupe performing in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' looks like 'cowardly' but strips the middle RRIB from TERRIBLE, leaving TE + LE; then CAST. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A telecast is a broadcast transmitted by television.

clue.text: Midday, and not a single person is lacking energy

indicators.note: is lacking says a letter is missing from the phrase

parts.note: no one means not a single person
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Lunchtime and nobody has any get-up-and-go.
explanation.walkthrough: NO ONE drops one E for energy; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock in the day, the middle of daylight hours.

clue.text: Adult friend touring ancient city

indicators.note: touring says the friend goes around the city

parts.note: mate is British for friend
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A grown-up pal visiting old ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts the friend around the city, as a visitor goes round a site; Ur is the Mesopotamian city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Mature means fully grown, as a grown-up is.

clue.text: Preserved in container, i.e. pickled?

definitions.meaning: food sealed in a tin is preserved
pickled is slang for drunk, as is the past form of tin-preserved

explanation.surface: Food kept in a jar, which is to say marinated in vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'i.e.' is a link. 'Pickled' looks like more food preserving, but here both words mean drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Food kept in tins is tinned; in slang the same word means drunk, which pickled also does.

clue.text: Ban sliced bread

indicators.note: sliced says the loaf's letters are cut up and reordered

explanation.surface: A prohibition on pre-cut loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to exclude or prohibit someone from something.

clue.text: Money collected in host's cap

indicators.note: collected says these letters are gathered together and put back in another order

explanation.surface: Coins gathered in the hat of the person hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HOST'S CAP, apostrophe S included, rearranged by 'collected'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot cash is ready money paid immediately on the spot.

clue.text: Church member's talisman

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A member of the congregation's lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a congregation member; it is a limb. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is an object believed to bring luck, as a talisman does.

clue.text: A fool rejected fish

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the two pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: nut is slang for a crazy person or fool

explanation.surface: An idiot spurned by a fishmonger.
explanation.walkthrough: A and NUT together, turned back by 'rejected', make TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish.

clue.text: Cyril Baker trained as a builder

indicators.note: trained says the letters of the name are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Cyril Baker learning a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges the ten letters of CYRIL BAKER; 'as a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer is a construction tradesman who lays bricks.

clue.text: Type of fuel available without charge after deal is arranged

indicators.note: after places the word for free behind the reordered letters
is arranged says the word deal has its letters reordered

parts.note: free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Petrol offered gratis once the contract is signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of fuel' is the definition; 'is arranged' reorders the four letters of 'deal', and 'after' sets the word for no charge behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded petrol contains no added lead, the metal once used as an additive.

clue.text: Weird Manx cat, perhaps, causing disturbance

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its end

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A strange tailless cat from the Isle of Man causing uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM plus PUS (PUSS made tailless, like a Manx cat, which is a breed from the Isle of Man with no tail); 'perhaps' and 'causing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or uproar.
